usageNotes: Use this to append a new firewall rule to the cluster-level ruleset, which applies globally across all nodes and VMs unless overridden at a lower scope. Requires the Sys.Modify privilege on the root path (/). Rules are inserted at the end of the list by default; supply 'pos' to insert at a specific zero-based position, which shifts existing rules down.

examples.summary: Block inbound SSH from a specific external subnet at the cluster level

params.comment: Block SSH brute-force attempts from known bad subnet

tips: The 'action' field accepts either a standard verdict (ACCEPT, DROP, REJECT) or the name of an existing security group — use the 'group' type when referencing a security group.
New rules are disabled by default (enable=0) unless you explicitly pass enable=1; always verify the rule is active after creation.
Use the 'digest' param when scripting back-to-back changes to guard against race conditions with concurrent edits.
Do not mix IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in the same 'source' or 'dest' field; use separate rules for each address family.
Cluster-level rules are evaluated before node- and VM-level rules; an overly broad DROP here can silently block traffic across the entire cluster.
